article_sentences: Three months of lull established by security forces in Jammu and Kashmir was rattled by the back-to-back incidents of violence in the past six days.
On November 11, a terror attack on a checkpoint manned by the personnel of the Central Reserve.
Police Force (CRPF) in Kulgam left three jawans injured.
On November 16, a local, whom the police suspected of having joined the terror ranks a few days ago, was killed after six days of a siege-like anti-terror operation in residential areas of Kulgam.
In Jammu’s Kishtwar, two Special.
Police Officers (SPOs) of the J&K. Police were found dead with bullet wounds, a day after they were reported missing in a forest range on November 11.
The police and the Army, however, remain tight-lipped about the circumstances around the killing of these SPOs, and there are conflicting reports on the circumstances that led to their deaths.
The anti-terror operation in civilian areas of Kulgam has raised concerns.

Former J&K Chief Minister and PDP president Mehbooba Mufti described the operation, spread over six days, as “collective punishment that only breeds alienation and resentment,” while NC spokesman Imran Nabi Dar suggested that entire villages were put under prolonged restrictions for days.
The Omar Abdullah government, because of limited powers and no jurisdiction over the police in J&K, a Union Territory since 2019, finds itself hamstrung.
The iron hand policy to stamp out terrorism and separatism has been effective from a strictly security perspective — terror attacks as well as local recruitments into terror ranks have declined.
According to the police, local recruits have come down to single digit or fewer than 10 in Kashmir.

stories.headline: Congress wants probe into conflicting versions in Kishtwar incident : Karra
stories.title: Congress wants probe into conflicting versions in Kishtwar incident : Karra
stories.summary: Jammu, Nov 17: Jammu and Kashmir Pradesh Congress Committee (JKPCC) president Tariq Hameed Karra on Tuesday reiterated that his party wanted probe into conflicting versions vis-a-vis two SPOs' killings in Kishtwar. “Congress objects to the way the BJP has questioned the integrity of Jammu and Kashmir Police (JKP) and used inappropriate words against it. They termed JKP as inefficient and good for nothing which brought down the morale of the entire force (JKP). Secondly, we object to the statements (of BJP leaders) referring to Masjid (mosque). We perceive these statements as attempts aimed at vitiating the atmosphere ahead of Punjab elections,” Karra alleged, while responding to media queries on the sidelines of a party function in Jammu. “You (media) need to ask them (BJP) leaders under what circumstances they made such statements which not only vitiated the atmosphere there (in Kishtwar) but would leave its impact across J&K,” he maintained. Responding to his (Karra's) statement that “SPOs had gone for hunting and were killed in the firing by Army probably due to mistaken identity”, JKPCC president denied having made any statement against the Army. “We did not raise any question about the Army. But what about the charges, they (BJP) have levelled against the Police. We only said that two versions emanated from there (Kishtwar) - one related to militants' angle and the second one related to the Army. We did not level any allegations. We simply said that it was the matter for investigation and all angles should be investigated,” Karra clarified. He also questioned the earlier claims of the central government declaring “Kishtwar-militancy free.” In response to a question about the Kulgam terror attack, followed by an encounter wherein a terrorist was killed, JKPCC president said that the questions on that account should be posed to Centre, MHA, Union Home Minister and the Prime Minister.

stories.headline: Thank you, Geethu: Malta PM praises Malayali nurse in parliament budget speech
stories.title: Thank you, Geethu: Malta PM praises Malayali nurse in parliament budget speech
stories.summary: During his budget address, Malta Prime Minister Robert Abela publicly thanked Keralite nurse Geethu Louis, praising her exceptional pandemic leadership and dedicated healthcare service to his family.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: In a heartfelt gesture highlighting the dedication of Indian healthcare professionals abroad, Malta Prime Minister Robert Abela expressed deep gratitude to a Keralite nurse during his budget address in parliament.
Commending her commitment, the Prime Minister acknowledged the crucial role foreign workers play in the nation’s growth and public welfare.
"When my father and mother fell ill, and when my daughter needed care, it was a foreign nurse who came to our aid.
Her name is Geethu.
Thank you, Geethu, we are indebted to your service," Prime Minister Abela remarked during his parliamentary speech.
The nurse, 35-year-old Geethu Louis, hails from Meloor near Chalakudy in Thrissur district.
Prior to moving to Malta in 2018, she worked as an operation theatre nurse in Keralam.
Her journey in the European nation took a pivotal turn during the height of the Covid-19 pandemic, when authorities sought healthcare workers willing to screen incoming passengers at the airport.
While many hesitated, Geethu stepped forward to take on the task.
Recognising her efficiency and courage, officials eventually entrusted her with leading Covid-19 testing operations across the country.
In this leadership role, she managed around 300 healthcare personnel across 32 hospital facilities, establishing herself as one of the most respected healthcare workers in Malta's government network.
Her exceptional reputation led to a personal assignment when former Malta President George Abela, the father of Prime Minister Robert Abela, suffered an injury in an accident.

stories.headline: Trump heads to China, betting on unscripted diplomacy with Xi and Putin
stories.title: Trump heads to China, betting on unscripted diplomacy with Xi and Putin
stories.summary: Shenzhen, Nov 18: President Donald Trump departs Wednesday for China, where he will participate in a historic trilateral meeting with that country's president, Xi Jinping, and Russian leader Vladimir Putin at a time when much of the world has been on edge because of the wars in Ukraine and Iran and the transformations wrought by artificial intelligence. The president has signalled that he wants to take an improvised approach to his time in Shenzhen, China, the skyscraper-filled tech hub that is hosting world leaders for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit. It's a bet that his unscripted brand of diplomacy based on personal relationships can create some kind of legacy to reshape world affairs during his final two years in the White House. Trump said he plans to talk with Xi and Putin about limiting nuclear weapons and bringing an end to the war in Ukraine, which began in 2022 with Russia's invasion. Analysts are not expecting substantive breakthroughs, despite the unprecedented nature of the meeting. Before the trip, Trump's aides had told reporters that the war in Ukraine would not be part of the trilateral meeting. Still, the president said on Tuesday that the deaths of tens of thousands of Russian troops every month had created an opening to resolve the conflict. "I think it's very close to getting it done," Trump said. "We're going to have a good meeting on that." Trump also teased the possibility of a private meeting with Putin and a separate sit-down with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, though neither event has been confirmed beyond the US president's own musings. "I don't know, but I would. If it's available, I would do that," Trump said Tuesday about talking on the sidelines with Putin. Trump said "We'll see what happens" on the prospect of meeting with Kim, whose nuclear arsenal is a threat to the US and its allies in Japan and South Korea. Trump said the North Korean leader would like to meet. Trump may have a reunion with Imelda Marcos The US president starts his day in the Philippine capital, Manila, where he may have a short reunion with Imelda Marcos, the former first lady, whose son is now president. Trump is having lunch with President Ferdinand Marcos Jr at the Malacanang Presidential Palace. Famed for her lavish shoe collection, Imelda Marcos knew Trump decades ago through the New York City party scene. During the 1986 "People Power" uprising, her husband, Ferdinand, was ousted as the Philippines' strongman leader. The meeting with the now 97-year-old former first lady depends on her doctors' approval. Trump on Tuesday met with leaders of the Quad alliance in Manila, signed a trade statement with Thailand and was feted at a formal dinner with Southeast Asian leaders. Trump plans to depart in the afternoon for Shenzhen, and he expressed excitement about the arrival ceremony that awaits him. "I am the guest of President Xi and I hear we're going to have quite a landing," he told reporters. "It's going to be a beautiful thing." The US president on Thursday will participate in the APEC summit and then hold his meeting with Xi and Putin, before then returning to the US. What's on the agenda for Trump's meetings with Xi and Putin The prospect of Trump meeting with two of America's largest geopolitical rivals has been a source of concern as the US president has been less welcoming of historic allies such as Canada and NATO partners in Europe. His tariffs that were intended to curb China's trade surplus have done little to stop the progress of the world's dominant manufacturer, which for the second straight year will have exported USD 1 trillion more in goods than what it imported. On Tuesday, Xi met with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and they agreed to further reduce tariffs on each other's goods. Carney has cultivated tighter economic ties with China and the European Union in response to strains in Canada's relationship with Trump, who at times has said he wants to make the country America's 51st state. Questions about how to handle AI also loom over the summit. The technology is viewed as key to unlocking faster economic growth, but its rapid development has meant it poses national security risks and could be beyond human control. Trump's close tech industry ally Jensen Huang was recently removed as the CEO of Nvidia after he admitted to an affair with a woman alleged to be an agent of the Chinese government. article_sentences: GUWAHATI: Even as there's a nip in the air, heralding the onset of winter season, the political debate seems to be heating up in Assam over the issue of National Register of Citizens (NRC).
The Supreme Court of India today admitted the petition filed by the All Assam Students' Union (AASU) seeking re-examination of the citizenship register.

While the state government has already made public its intent to approach the Supreme Court seeking revision of the final draft of NRC published in 2019, the AASU has gone a step further in already filing a petition before the apex court seeking re-examination of the register.
A division bench of Justice P Srinarasimha and Justice Alok Aradhe issued notices to the Central and Assam governments on Tuesday seeking their response on the matter.
AASU president Utpal Sarma said the student body approached the Supreme Court seeking an error-free NRC, since the entire exercise was carried out under the supervision of the apex court.

He alleged that lots of discrepancies had crept into the final draft of NRC due to laxity of the then state government, pointing out that names of 40 lakh individuals were dropped from the first draft, before that number dropped to 19 lakh in the final draft.
Sarma said the AASU is not satisfied with the fact that names of only 19 lakh individuals were left out from the final draft after spending so much of money.
Around Rs 1,600 crore was reportedly spent in undertaking the entire exercise.
"Even the current state government said that it was not satisfied with the outcome, but still has not approached the Supreme Court seeking NRC revision.
This compelled AASU to approach the apex court, which admitted our plea and issued notices to both Delhi and Dispur.
They will now have to file replies to the court on the matter," he elaborated.
As reported in The Sentinel earlier, Dispur was now opting for a complete revision of the final NRC before the Supreme Court.

article_sentences: New Delhi: The Supreme Court on Tuesday asked Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut and journalist Nikhil Wagle to appear physically on December 8 in a criminal contempt case over their remarks against Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and the judiciary.

A bench of Justice Aravind Kumar and Justice Vipul M Pancholi pulled up Raut over his subsequent social media posts criticising the judiciary despite having tendered an apology for his earlier remarks, observing that an apology in a matter of such magnitude must come "from the heart and not the mind".

The apex court was hearing a criminal contempt petition filed by the Supreme Court Bar Association (SCBA) against Raut and Wagle over their alleged objectionable remarks against the CJI and the judiciary.

Referring to his posts alleging that the BJP had brought the judiciary, central investigating agencies and the Election Commission under its control, Rai also cited a photograph shared by Raut showing protesters setting fire to Albania's Supreme Court.
Describing Raut as a "habitual offender", Rai urged the bench to deal with the matter with an "iron hand".

article_sentences: The Maharashtra Cabinet, chaired by Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) approved four proposals, including amendments to the Maharashtra Public Universities Act, 2016, changes to the State’s textile policy, the establishment of new courts in Palghar and a cash reward scheme for information leading to the recovery of weapons looted by Maoists from security forces.

The Cabinet approved a draft ordinance to amend Sections 13(12) and 100(5)(a) of the Maharashtra Public Universities Act, 2016, in view of changes in higher education and the implementation of the National Education Policy, 2020.
Under the proposed amendments, the Chancellor of a State university will be empowered to remove a Pro-Vice-Chancellor on the recommendation of the Vice-Chancellor concerned.
The changes will also allow university construction and development works to be undertaken through the Public Works Department under the supervision of the university’s Management Council.
The Cabinet also approved amendments to the Integrated and Sustainable Textile Policy, 2023–28, bringing Palghar district under Zone 1 owing to its tribal district status.
The revised policy abolishes Zone 4 and reclassifies districts across the remaining three zones.

The amendments also redefine expansion of textile projects, allowing the installation of additional machinery valued at 10% or more of the previous financial year’s machinery book value to qualify as expansion.

Eligible projects that received loan approvals or made advance payments for machinery before June 1, 2023, but commenced production during the new policy period, will be allowed to choose benefits under either the 2018–23 or 2023–28 policy.

In another decision, the Cabinet approved the establishment of a Principal District and Sessions Court and a Chief Judicial Magistrate’s Court in Palghar, along with a District Government Pleader’s Office.

The decision follows approval by the Bombay High Court’s committee for establishing new courts to create a separate judicial district for Palghar, which was carved out of Thane district in August 2014.

The government approved the creation of 100 new posts across the two courts and the government pleader’s office, along with the transfer of 29 existing posts and engagement of outsourced personnel for 43 positions.
The Cabinet also approved a cash reward scheme for individuals providing information that helps authorities recover weapons looted by Maoists from security forces.

stories.headline: IUST hosts national conference on emerging technologies
stories.title: IUST hosts national conference on emerging technologies
stories.summary: Awantipora, Nov 17: The Islamic University of Science and Technology (IUST) commenced its two-day National Conference on ‘Emerging Technologies for Governance and Development Planning in Jammu and Kashmir: Policy and Implementation’ on Tuesday. The conference is being organised by the Centre for Good Governance and Policy Analysis (CGG&PA), IUST, in collaboration with the Centre for Good Governance (CGG), Hyderabad, and the Information Technology Department, Government of Jammu and Kashmir. Minister for Health, Medical Education and Social Welfare, J&K, Sakina Masood Itoo, who graced the occasion as chief guest, said, technology can make government services more transparent and accessible, especially in the health sector, where difficult terrain and seasonal cut-offs hinder timely care. Digital systems, she said, can map remote habitations, track ambulances, flag high-risk pregnancies, enable tele-consultation and ensure early detection of outbreaks. She said, while e-UNNAT with 1500+ services denotes a significant progress, digital governance must ensure accountability beyond online availability. She added that Artificial Intelligence can assist doctors in diagnosis in underserved areas, but must not replace human supervision with strict protection of patient data. “Universities must go beyond classrooms to become centres of research and innovation, collaborating with departments and hospitals to develop practical solutions for J&K,” she said. Itoo also inaugurated the Faculty Residential Quarters at IUST Main Campus. Speaking on the occasion, Prof. Shakil Ahmad Romshoo, Vice Chancellor, IUST, highlighted that the Centre for Good Governance and Policy Analysis, established just a year ago, has emerged as one of the University's most vibrant and proactive centres, fostering meaningful engagement between academia and policymaking. Expressing confidence that the two-day conference would generate valuable insights, institutional partnerships and practical policy recommendations, Prof. Romshoo emphasised, “The conference must culminate in a focused and actionable Policy and Implementation Roadmap for Technology-Enabled Governance in J&K, identifying high-impact interventions that can be piloted, evaluated and scaled across departments and districts.” He further underscored, “Our vision must be a Jammu and Kashmir where every village, institution and citizen benefits from intelligent, inclusive and sustainable governance, with technology serving as an instrument of transparency, accountability and equitable development.” In his special remarks, Ravi Gupta, IPS (Rtd.), Executive Vice President and Director General, Centre for Good Governance (CGG), Hyderabad, said, emerging technologies such as AI, ML, deep learning and cloud can help identify systemic gaps, check collusive corruption and trace money trails while protecting honest officers. He stressed that citizens trust government with their personal data and that it is incumbent upon government to keep it secure. Patron, IIPA Jammu and member, National Security Advisory Board, Ashok Bhan, IPS (Rtd.), said, good governance must be achieved through optimum utilization of available resources, catalysed by technology, innovation and change, with an ecosystem built on transparency, accountability, zero tolerance to corruption and citizen centricity. He stressed that citizens must be taken on board in initiatives like smart cities, with technology used to capture aspirations and build capacity to use services. He noted that grievance redressal models like Sevottam, though well-conceived, remain rule-bound and lack empathy, and called for systems combining technological efficiency with human sensitivity. Earlier, Dr. G. N. Itoo, Director, CGG&PA presented the welcome address and set the context for the conference. The formal vote of thanks was proposed by Prof. Shamim Ahmad Shah, Registrar, IUST. The inaugural session held at Lal Ded auditorium of IUST also featured screening of a documentary featuring achievements of IUST and CGG&PA. Following the inaugural session, various technical sessions were held at the Conference Hall, Rumi Library. To mention, the two-day conference aims to deliberate on policy frameworks and implementation strategies for leveraging emerging technologies to strengthen good governance and development planning in J&K. The conference has been sponsored by the Information Technology Department, Government of J&K, and Jammu and Kashmir Bank Ltd, and Renewable Energy Pvt. Ltd.

stories.headline: Tenders, Environmental Laws, and Design Thinking Approach
stories.title: Tenders, Environmental Laws, and Design Thinking Approach
stories.summary: For several generations Mohammad Akbar has been catching fish from Sukhnag stream. This 64 year fisherman from Arwah village in Beerwah tehsil of Central Kashmir’s Budgam District has been into this profession for last more than 40 years. He has inherited it from his parents and grandparents. Sukhnag stream is known for its trout and traditional Kashmiri fish and has been designated as a trout stream by J&K Fisheries Department. Sukhnag is a tributary of the Jhelum, originating from the glaciers of the Pir Panjal mountains and flowing through many villages of Beerwah. For last 5 to 6 years the livelihood of Mohammad Akbar and many other fishermen has been directly impacted? The catch is less as there has been large scale riverbed mining taking place in Sukhnag in around one dozen villages. This author fought this mining mafia in National Green Tribunal-NGT. For last almost 2 years the illegal excavation of boulders, sand and gravel with heavy machinery has been halted to a great extent as NGT has imposed ban on this illegal trade from last almost 2 years now. After the mining ban Sukhnag was reviving day by day and population of fish was also growing, but another human induced disaster has snatched livelihood of Akbar and many of his colleagues. Halting Fish Movement ? Around the autumn of 2024 Govt constructed a concrete structure in the middle of Sukhnag at village Makhama which is around 7kms downstream of Beerwah town. The structure was meant for “protection” of abutments of the bridge but this structure has caused huge loss to the fishermen community. The upward movement of fish has been hampered and fishermen like Mohammad Akbar are not even able to catch 1 kg of fish a day? Mohammad Akbar has to take care of 8 members of family which includes his wife and six daughters. He is not able to do other job due to old age? I, along with my colleagues of J&K Climate Action Group-JKCAG, on November 1st 2026 visited Makhama to meet these aggrieved fishermen. We met around two dozen fishermen and they informed us that there are around 200 families who have been impacted. When the construction work was taken up the concerned departments (PWD, R&B) didn’t consult Fisheries Department or Flood control department. Fisheries Department’s official letter to R&B The Assistant Director Fisheries, Budgam wrote an official letter to Executive Engineer R&B Division Beerwah on 3.04.2025 and advised the department not to go ahead with the construction work as this would severely impact the livelihood of fishermen community (Mahigeers). The official communication reads: “As already discussed telephonically, it is once again reiterated that this office has received a representation from the registered fishermen of Circle Beerwa regarding the construction of an embankment in Nallah Sukhnag under the bridge at Makhama Village. In this regard, it is to state that the fishermen residing in the area are wholly and solely dependent on this Nallah for their daily livelihood by means of catching fish. The construction of the said embankment will definitely result in declining fish production by way of hindering the fish movement upstream, thereby jeopardizing the livelihood of the fishermen. The construction of an embankment across the river will prove very detrimental for the breeding and sustainability of the fish fauna as per the Fisheries regulations. Pertinent to mention here that the only source of income to these fishermen comes from the catch of fish in the Nallah, and if their genuine demand is not considered seriously, it will badly affect their livelihood and also the sustainability of the river “ The R&B Division also didn’t get a No Objection Certificate-NOC from concerned Flood Control Department. I spoke to Mr. Javed Kurpal, Executive Engineer of the Flood Spill Channel Division Narbal, and he confirmed that NOC was not given by them for the construction. Flawed Notice Inviting Tender -NIT I am unable to understand why the Notice Inviting Tenders-NITs are flawed on many occasions as environmental aspect is not taken into consideration. I had written a detailed piece on that, and uploaded videos on social media as well. The work was halted but in Pirbagh area the trees are now choked in concrete. No Empathy for Fishermen? Similarly, if the R&B Division has plans to protect abutments of Makhama bridge, why didn’t they think of Fishermen community? Why didn’t they respect the National Water Policy and J&K Water Resources (Regulation and Management Act ) Act 2010. Both of them have been violated. The fact of the matter is that engineers hardly visit the site. The contractor does what he wants. When Fishermen resisted, contractor got them booked and they were put inside the lockup. Our Govt talks about “Design Thinking” which is now part of our National Education Policy. The core value of Design Thinking is based on Empathy and this is missing in our Govt sector especially when we execute the Govt works on the ground? Empathy is the core starting point of design thinking. It is the practice of understanding the people you are designing for, setting aside your own assumptions, and seeing the world through their eyes. I ask the Executive Engineer R&B Division Beerwah; did you prepare the NIT of Makhama bridge using Design Thinking principles? Why was empathy towards Fishermen missing? This is not enough; the Fishermen who have been impacted for last almost 2 years should be compensated as well by the government. Conclusion I appeal authorities especially Chief Engineers of PWD (R&B), PHE Irrigation, UEED, and KPDCL to make sure they prepare all the NITs in consonance with Environmental Laws and by respecting the design thinking principles- especially empathy, ideation and multi-disciplinary approach. The Engineering Departments especially must consult environmental experts while preparing tender documents (NITs). Furthermore, all engineering construction divisions must have an Environmental Engineer or Environmental Consultant position to examine the tender documents before they are issued. Dr Raja Muzaffar Bhat is an Acumen Fellow. He is Chairman J&K Climate Action Group & Founder of J&K RTI Movement

Sukhnag is a tributary of the Jhelum, originating from the glaciers of the Pir Panjal mountains and flowing through many villages of Beerwah.
For last 5 to 6 years the livelihood of Mohammad Akbar and many other fishermen has been directly impacted?
The catch is less as there has been large scale riverbed mining taking place in Sukhnag in around one dozen villages.
This author fought this mining mafia in National Green Tribunal-NGT.

The upward movement of fish has been hampered and fishermen like Mohammad Akbar are not even able to catch 1 kg of fish a day?

He is not able to do other job due to old age?
